desc_content.paragraph: An abstraction over Hydra’s store, for creating multiple, isolated config stores.

Whereas Hydra exposes a single global config store that provides no warnings when store entries are overwritted, ZenStore instances are isolated, do not populate the global store unless instructed to, and they protect users from unwittingly overwriting store entries.

definition.paragraph: Returns a sorted list of the groups registered with this store

Internally, each ZenStore instance holds a mapping of:

ZenStore is also designed to consolidate the config-creation and storage process; it can be used to automatically apply config-creation a function (e.g., builds) to a target in order to auto-generate a config for the target, which is then stored.

container.literal_block:
from hydra_zen import store def func(x, y): ...
store(func, x=2, y=3)

from hydra_zen import builds, store def func(x, y): ...
store(builds(func, x=2, y=3, populate_full_signature=True), name="func")

desc_content.paragraph: It can also be used to decorate config-targets and dataclasses, enabling “inline” config creation and storage patterns.

These auto config-creation capabilities are designed to be deferred until a config is actually accessed by users or added to Hydra’s global config store. This enables store-decorator patterns to be used within library code without slowing down import times.

A ZenStore instance can be called repeatedly - without a config target - with different options to incrementally change the store’s default configurations. E.g. the following are effectively equivalent

container.literal_block:
from hydra_zen import store
book_store = store(group="books") romance_store = book_store(provider="genre: romance") fantasy_store = book_store(provider="genre: fantasy")
romance_store({"title": "heartfelt"}) romance_store({"title": "lustfully longingness"})
fantasy_store({"title": "elvish cookbook"}) fantasy_store({"title": "dwarves can't jump"})

from hydra_zen import store
store( {"title": "heartfelt"}, group="book", provider="genre: romance", ) store( {"title": "lustfully longingness"}, group="book", provider="genre: romance", )
store( {"title": "elvish cookbook"}, group="book", provider="genre: fantasy", ) store( {"title": "dwarves can't jump"}, group="book", provider="genre: fantasy", )

desc_content.paragraph: Special support is provided for overriding Hydra’s configuration; the name and group of the store entry is inferred to be ‘config’ and ‘hydra’, respectively, when an instance/subclass of HydraConf is being stored. E.g., specifying
desc_content.literal_block:
from hydra.conf import HydraConf, JobConf from hydra_zen import store
store(HydraConf(job=JobConf(chdir=True)))
desc_content.paragraph: is equivalent to writing the following manually
Additionally, overwriting the store entry for HydraConf will not raise an error even if ZenStore(overwrite_ok=False) is specified.
(Some helpful boilerplate code for these examples)
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import to_yaml, store, ZenStore >>> def pyaml(x): ... # for pretty printing configs ... print(to_yaml(x))
desc_content.paragraph: Let’s add a config to hydra-zen’s pre-instantiated ZenStore instance. Each store entry must have an associated name. Optionally, a group, package, and/or provider may be specified for the entry as well.
A store’s entries are keyed by their (group, name) pairs (the default group is None).
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store["profiles", "roger"] # (group, name) -> config node {'name': 'Roger', age: 24}
desc_content.paragraph: By default, the stored config(s) will be “enqueued” for addition to Hydra’s config store. The method add_to_hydra_store() must be called to add the enqueued configs to Hydra’s central store.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store.has_enqueued() True >>> store.add_to_hydra_store() # adds all enqueued entries to Hydra's global store >>> store.has_enqueued() False
desc_content.paragraph: By default, attempting to overwrite an entry will result in an error.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store({}, name="rita", group="profiles") # same name and group as above ValueError: (name=rita group=profiles): Hydra config store entry already exists. Specify `overwrite_ok=True` to enable replacing config store entries
desc_content.paragraph: We can create a distinct store that has an independent internal repository of configs.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> new_store = ZenStore("new_store") >>> _ = new_store([1, 2, 3], name="backbone")
desc_content.paragraph: The input to a store is processed by the store’s to_config function prior to creating the stored config node. This defaults to hydra_zen.wrapper.default_to_config, which applies hydra_zen.builds or hydra_zen.just to inputs based on their types.
For instance, consider the following function:
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> def sum_it(a: int, b: int): return a + b
desc_content.paragraph: We can pass sum_it directly to our store to leverage auto-config and auto-naming capabilities. Here, builds(sum_it, a=1, b=2) will be called under the hood by new_store to create the config for sum_it.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store2 = ZenStore() >>> _ = store2(sum_it, a=1, b=2) # entry name defaults to `sum_it.__name__` >>> config = store2[None, "sum_it"] >>> pyaml(config) _target_: __main__.sum_it a: 1 b: 2
desc_content.paragraph: Refer to hydra_zen.wrapper.default_to_config for more details about the default auto-config behaviors of ZenStore.
ZenStore.__call__ is a pass-through and can be used as a decorator. Let’s add two store entries for func by decorating it.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store = ZenStore()
>>> @store(a=1, b=22, name="func1") ... @store(a=-10, name="func2") ... def func(a: int, b: int): ... return a - b
desc_content.paragraph: Each application of @store utilizes the store’s auto-config capability to create and store a config inline. I.e. the above snippet is equivalent to
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import builds >>> >>> store(builds(func, a=1, b=22), name="func1") >>> store(builds(func, a=-10, ... populate_full_signature=True ... ), ... name="func2", ... )
>>> func(10, 3) # the decorated function is left unchanged 7 >>> pyaml(store[None, "func1"]) _target_: __main__.func a: 1 b: 22 >>> pyaml(store[None, "func2"]) _target_: __main__.func b: ??? a: -10
desc_content.paragraph: Note that, by default, the application of to_config via the store is deferred until that entry is actually accessed. This offsets the runtime cost of constructing configs for the decorated function so that it need not be paid until the config is actually accessed by the store.

The default values for a store’s __call__ parameters – group, to_config, etc. – can easily be customized. Simply call the store with those new values and without specifying an object to be stored. This will return a “mirrored” store instance – with the same internal state as the original store – with updated defaults.
For example, let’s create a store where we want to store multiple configs under a 'math' group and under a 'functools' group, respectively.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> import math >>> import functools
>>> new_store = ZenStore() >>> math_store = new_store(group="math") # overwrites group default >>> tool_store = new_store(group="functools") # overwrites group default
desc_content.paragraph: math_store and tool_store both share the same internal state as new_store, but have overwritten default values for the group.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> math_store(math.floor) # equivalent to: `new_store(math.floor, group="math")` >>> math_store(math.ceil) >>> tool_store(functools.lru_cache) >>> tool_store(functools.wraps)
desc_content.paragraph: See that new_store has entries under these corresponding groups:
These “self-partialing” patterns can be chained indefinitely and can be used to set partial defaults for the to_config function.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> profile_store = new_store(group="profile") >>> schemaless = profile_store(schema="<none>")

>>> from dataclasses import dataclass >>> >>> @profile_store(name="admin", has_root=True) >>> @schemaless(name="test_admin", has_root=True) >>> @schemaless(name="test_user", has_root=False) >>> @dataclass >>> class Profile: >>> username: str >>> schema: str >>> has_root: bool
>>> pyaml(new_store["profile", "admin"]) username: ??? schema: ??? has_root: true _target_: __main__.Profile
>>> pyaml(new_store["profile", "test_admin"]) username: ??? schema: <none> has_root: true _target_: __main__.Profile
desc_content.paragraph: A store can be copied, updated, and merged. Its entries can have their groups remapped, and individual entries can be deleted. See the docs for the corresponding methods for details and examples.

definition.paragraph: The name for this store.
If True (default), this store will a not apply to_config to the target until that specific entry is accessed by the store.
If True (default), this store will not add entries to Hydra’s global config store until store.add_to_hydra_store is called explicitly.
If False (default), attempting to overwrite entries in this store and trying to use this store to overwrite entries in Hydra’s global store will raise a ValueError.
If True specifying a node kwarg in ZenStore.__call__ will emit a warning.
This helps to protect users from mistakenly self-partializing a store with store(node=Config) instead of actually storing the node with store(Config).

desc_parameterlist.desc_parameter: target : Optional[T] = None, /, name: NodeName | Callable[[Any], NodeName]] = ..., group: GroupName | Callable[[T], GroupName]] = None, package: Optional[str | Callable[[T], str]]] | None], provider: Optional[str], to_config: Callable[[T], Node] = ..., **to_config_kw: Any

desc_content.paragraph: Store a config or customize the default values of the store.

definition.paragraph: The object to be stored. This is a positional-only argument.
If obj is not specified, then the provided arguments are used to create a mirrored store instance with updated default arguments.
The entry’s name, or a callable that will be called as (obj) -> entry-name. The default is lambda obj: obj.__name__.
Store entries are keyed off of (group, name).
The entry’s group’s name, or a callable that will be called as (obj) -> entry-group. The default is None. Subgroups can be specified using / within the group name.
Store entries are keyed off of (group, name).

Called on obj to produce the entry’s “node” (the config). Refer to hydra_zen.wrapper.default_to_config for the default behavior. Specify lambda x: x to have obj be stored directly as the entry’s node.
By default the call to to_config is deferred until the entry is actually accessed by the store.
The entry’s package. Default is None.
An optional provider name for the entry.
Additional arguments that will be passed to to_config.
If obj was specified, it is returned unchanged. Otherwise a new instance of ZenStore is return, which mirrors the internal state of this store and has updated default arguments.

desc_content.paragraph: Access a entry’s config node by specifying (group, name). Or, access a mapping of (group, name) -> node for all nodes in a specified group, including nodes within subgroups.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import store >>> store(dict(x=1), name="a", group="fruit") >>> store(dict(x=2), name="b", group="fruit/apple") >>> store(dict(x=3), name="c", group="fruit/apple") >>> store(dict(x=4), name="d", group="fruit/orange") >>> store(dict(x=5), name="e", group="veggie")
desc_content.paragraph: Accessing an individual entry’s config node.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store["fruit/apple", "b"] {'x': 2}
desc_content.paragraph: Accessing all config nodes under the “fruit/apple” group
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store["fruit/apple"] {('fruit/apple', 'b'): {'x': 2}, ('fruit/apple', 'c'): {'x': 3}}
desc_content.paragraph: Accessing all config nodes under the “fruit” group
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> store["fruit"] {('fruit', 'a'): {'x': 1}, ('fruit/apple', 'b'): {'x': 2}, ('fruit/apple', 'c'): {'x': 3}, ('fruit/orange', 'd'): {'x': 4}}

desc_content.paragraph: Adds all of this store’s enqueued entries to Hydra’s global config store.
This method need not be called for a store initialized as ZenStore(deferred_hydra_store=False).

definition.paragraph: If False, this method raises ValueError if an entry in Hydra’s config store will be overwritten. Defaults to the value of overwrite_ok specified when initializing this store.

desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> store1 = ZenStore() >>> store2 = ZenStore()

>>> store1({'a': 1}, name="x") >>> store1.add_to_hydra_store() >>> store2({'a': 2}, name="x") >>> store2.add_to_hydra_store() ValueError: (name=x group=None): Hydra config store entry already exists. Specify `overwrite_ok=True` to enable replacing config store entries
>>> store2.add_to_hydra_store(overwrite_ok=True) # successfully overwrites entry

desc_content.paragraph: Returns a copy of the store with the same overridden defaults.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> s1 = ZenStore()(group="G") >>> s1({}, name="a") >>> s2 = s1.copy() >>> s2({}, name="b") >>> s1 s1 {'G': ['a']} >>> s2 s1_copy {'G': ['a', 'b']}

desc_content.paragraph: Create a copy of a store whose entries’ groups have been updated according to the provided mapping.

definition.paragraph: A mapping or callable that transforms an old group name to a new one. Groups in the store that are not included in the mapping are unaffected.
A GroupName is str | None.
If specified, the name of the new store.
If specified, determines if the mapping can overwrite existing store entries. Otherwise, defers to ZenStore(overwrite_ok).
A copy of self with remapped groups.

desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore
desc_content.paragraph: Creating an initial store
Replacing group “A/1” with “B”, via a mapping
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> s2 = s1.copy_with_mapped_groups({"A/1": "B"}, store_name="s2") >>> s2 s2 {None: ['a'], 'A/2': ['c'], 'B': ['b']}
desc_content.paragraph: Placing all entries under group “A/” within a new inner group “p”, via a function
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> s3 = s1.copy_with_mapped_groups( ... lambda g: g + "/p" if g and g.startswith("A/") else g, store_name="s3" ... ) >>> s3 s3 {None: ['a'], 'A/1/p': ['b'], 'A/2/p': ['c']}

desc_content.paragraph: Access a store entry, which is a mapping that specifies the entry’s name, group, package, provider, and node.
Mutating the returned mapping will not affect the store’s internal entry. Mutating a node in the returned entry may have unintended consequences and is not advised.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import store, ZenStore >>> store(dict(x=1), name="a", group="fruit") >>> store.get_entry("fruit", "a") {'name': 'a', 'group': 'fruit', 'package': None, 'provider': None, 'node': {'x': 1}}

desc_content.paragraph: Updates the store inplace with redundant entries being overwritten.
Can also be applied via the |= in-place operator.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> def f(): ... >>> def g(): ... >>> s1 = ZenStore("s1") >>> s2 = ZenStore("s2") >>> s1(f) # store f in s1 >>> s2(g) # store g in s2
>>> s1.update(s2) >>> s1 # s1 now has entries for both f and g s1 {None: ['f', 'g']}
desc_content.paragraph: Alternatively, the |= operator can be used to update a store inplace.
Create a new store by merging two stores.
The new store’s default settings will reflect those of self in self.merge(other). This can also be applied via the | operator.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> def f(): ... >>> def g(): ... >>> s1 = ZenStore("s1") >>> s2 = ZenStore("s2") >>> s1(f) # store f in s1 >>> s2(g) # store g in s2
>>> s3 = s1.merge(s2) >>> s3 s1_copy {None: ['f', 'g']}
desc_content.paragraph: Alternatively, the | operator can be used to merge stores.
True if this store has entries that have not yet been added to Hydra’s config store.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> store = ZenStore(deferred_hydra_store=True) >>> store.has_enqueued() False
>>> store({"a": 1}, name) >>> store.has_enqueued() True
>>> store.add_to_hydra_store() >>> store.has_enqueued() False

desc_content.paragraph: Add all of the store’s entries to the queue to be added to hydra’s store.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> store = ZenStore(deferred_hydra_store=True) >>> store({"a": 1}, name) >>> store.has_enqueued() True
>>> store.add_to_hydra_store() >>> store.has_enqueued() False
>>> store.enqueue_all() >>> store.has_enqueued() True

desc_content.paragraph: Yields all entries in this store.
Mutating the returned mappings will not affect the store’s internal entries. Mutating a node in an entry may have unintended consequences and is not advised.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import store >>> store(dict(x=1), name="a", group="fruit") >>> store(dict(x=2), name="b", group="fruit/orange") >>> store(dict(x=3), name="c", group="veggie")

>>> list(store) [{'name': 'a', 'group': 'fruit', 'package': None, 'provider': None, 'node': {'x': 1}}, {'name': 'b', 'group': 'fruit/orange', 'package': None, 'provider': None, 'node': {'x': 2}}, {'name': 'c', 'group': 'veggie', 'package': None, 'provider': None, 'node': {'x': 3}}]

desc_content.paragraph: Returns True if two stores share identical internal repos and queues.
desc_content.doctest_block: >>> from hydra_zen import ZenStore >>> store1 = ZenStore() >>> store2 = ZenStore() >>> store1_a = store1(group='a') >>> _ = store1_a(dict(x=1), name="foo")
>>> store1 == store1_a True >>> store1 == store2 False
